recipes.title: Coq au Vin (Chicken Braised in Red Wine)
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of Coq au Vin — chicken braised in red wine with pearl onions and mushrooms in a deep glossy sauce
recipes.prep_label: Served — Coq au Vin over Buttered Tagliatelle
recipes.prep_alt: Coq au Vin chicken pieces and sauce served over a bed of buttered tagliatelle with parsley

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the chicken dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
In a Dutch oven or heavy pot, cook the bacon lardons over medium heat until crisp and the fat has rendered, about 5 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat behind.
Sear the chicken skin-side down in the bacon fat until deeply browned, 4-5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside with the bacon.
Add the pearl onions and mushrooms to the pot, cooking 5-6 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic and carrot, cooking 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
If flambéing, return the chicken and bacon to the pot, warm the brandy separately, pour it over, and carefully ignite, letting the flames subside on their own.
Add the wine, stock, bay leaf, and thyme, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer gently 40-45 minutes (or braise in a 160°C/325°F oven) until the chicken is very tender.

Lift out the chicken, onions, and mushrooms and keep warm. Mash the butter and flour together into a smooth paste (beurre manié), then whisk it into the simmering sauce and cook 5 minutes until thickened.
Return the chicken and vegetables to the pot to coat in the sauce.
Garnish with parsley and serve hot with crusty bread, mashed potatoes, or buttered tagliatelle.

recipes.title: Ratatouille
recipes.dish_alt: A pot of finished ratatouille — stewed eggplant, zucchini, peppers, and tomatoes glistening with olive oil and fresh parsley
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Vegetables Going into the Pot
recipes.prep_alt: Chopped eggplant, zucchini, bell peppers, onion, and herbs in a pan at the start of cooking ratatouille

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cut the eggplant, zucchini, squash, and peppers into even 2cm chunks. Salt the eggplant and let it sit 15 minutes to draw out bitterness, then pat dry.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet or pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the eggplant and cook 5-6 minutes, stirring, until it starts to soften and color.
Add the zucchini and squash, cooking 5 minutes more.
Add the peppers and cook 3-4 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, herbes de Provence, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer gently 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender but still hold their shape.
Uncover and simmer 5 minutes more if there's excess liquid to cook off.
Discard the bay leaf, stir in the torn basil, and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Beef Bourguignon
recipes.dish_alt: A plated serving of Beef Bourguignon — red-wine-braised beef with pearl onions, mushrooms, and mashed potatoes
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Beef & Vegetables Simmering in the Pot
recipes.prep_alt: A pot of beef, carrots, onions, and mushrooms simmering together in red wine sauce for Beef Bourguignon

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the beef dry and season with salt and pepper.
In a Dutch oven, cook the bacon over medium heat until crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat in the pot.
Sear the beef in batches in the bacon fat until deeply browned on all sides; remove and set aside.
Add the chopped onion and carrot to the pot, cooking 5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in the flour and cook 1-2 minutes to coat the vegetables.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Return the beef and bacon to the pot, add the wine and stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add the bay leaf and thyme and bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer gently on low heat (or braise in a 160°C/325°F oven) 1½-2 hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Meanwhile, sauté the pearl onions and mushrooms in the butter in a separate pan until browned; set aside.
Stir the browned onions and mushrooms into the stew for the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Discard the bay leaf and thyme sprig, and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with parsley and serve with mashed potatoes, egg noodles, or crusty bread.

recipes.title: Quiche Lorraine
recipes.dish_alt: A whole Quiche Lorraine fresh from the oven with a golden, gently domed custard top in a glass pie dish
recipes.prep_label: Served — Sliced with a Side Salad
recipes.prep_alt: A slice of Quiche Lorraine plated with a dressed green salad

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Roll out the pie dough and fit it into a tart pan or pie dish, then prick the base all over with a fork.
Blind bake: line the crust with parchment and pie weights, bake 12-15 minutes, remove the weights, then bake 5 minutes more until lightly golden. Reduce the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp; remove and drain.
In the same fat, cook the onion 4-5 minutes until softened; drain off excess fat.
Scatter the bacon, onion, and Gruyère over the base of the crust.
Whisk together the eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the filling in the crust.
Bake 30-35 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight jiggle in the center and the top is golden.
Let cool 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Poulet Provençal (Provençal Chicken)
recipes.dish_alt: Chicken thighs braised with tomatoes and purple olives in a skillet, Provençal-style
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Chicken Simmering with Tomatoes & Peppers
recipes.prep_alt: Chicken pieces simmering in a pot with tomatoes, bell peppers, and garlic for Poulet Provençal

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken skin-side down 5-6 minutes until golden, flip, and sear 3 minutes more. Remove.
Add the onion to the pan and cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and bell peppers, cooking 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the white wine, scraping up any browned bits, and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, olives, and herbes de Provence.
Return the chicken to the pan, skin-side up, nestling it into the sauce.
Cover and simmer 25-30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Uncover and simmer 5 minutes more to thicken the sauce slightly.
Garnish with basil or parsley and serve with crusty bread or rice.

recipes.title: Salade Niçoise
recipes.dish_alt: A composed Salade Niçoise with tuna, egg, olives, tomatoes, and green beans arranged on a platter
recipes.prep_alt: Tuna, egg, olives, tomatoes, green beans, and greens tossed together for Salade Niçoise

sections.heading: Steps
items: Boil the potatoes in salted water 12-15 minutes until fork-tender. Drain, cool slightly, and halve.
Blanch the green beans in boiling salted water 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender, then shock in ice water and drain.
Boil the eggs 8-9 minutes for jammy centers (or 10 minutes for fully set), cool in ice water, peel, and halve.
Whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper together to make the vinaigrette.
Arrange the lettuce on a platter or individual plates.
Top with the potatoes, green beans, cherry tomatoes, red onion, and flaked tuna.
Add the halved eggs, olives, and anchovy fillets if using.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette just before serving.

recipes.title: Croque Monsieur
recipes.dish_alt: A golden, bubbling Croque Monsieur sandwich topped with melted béchamel and cheese
recipes.prep_alt: A Croque Monsieur sliced in half and served on a plate with a fresh green salad and mustard dip

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the béchamel: melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour, and cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and cook, whisking, 3-4 minutes until thickened. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Spread one side of each bread slice with Dijon mustard.
Layer the ham and half the Gruyère between two mustard-spread bread slices to make a sandwich.
Spread a layer of béchamel over the top of the sandwich and sprinkle with the remaining Gruyère.
Toast in a skillet with a little butter, or bake at 220°C (425°F) for 8-10 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
For a Croque Madame, top with a fried egg before serving — an easy variation.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Crème Brûlée (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: A ramekin of Crème Brûlée with a caramelized sugar top and a dollop of whipped cream
recipes.prep_alt: A ramekin of crème brûlée being caramelized under an open flame from a kitchen torch

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F).
Heat the cream with the vanilla in a saucepan until just steaming — do not let it boil.
Whisk the egg yolks and sugar together until pale.
Slowly whisk the hot cream into the yolk mixture in a thin stream to temper it.
Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into a jug to remove any bits.
Divide among ramekins, place in a baking dish, and pour hot water halfway up the sides to make a water bath.
Bake 30-35 minutes until the custards are set around the edges but still slightly jiggly in the center.
Remove from the water bath, cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours (or overnight).
Just before serving, sprinkle an even layer of sugar over each custard.
Caramelize with a kitchen torch until deep amber and crisp (or under a hot broiler, watching closely).
Let sit 1-2 minutes for the sugar to harden, then serve immediately.
